sections.title: Bone Composition
points: Bones are living tissues. They have blood vessels, nerves, and living cells.
They are the hardest tissue in the body because they store Calcium and Phosphorus.
Bones need proper feeding and nutrients to stay strong.

sections.title: Internal Parts of a Bone
points: Hard Bone: The outer layer that provides strength and protects the marrow.
Spongy Bone: The porous part found at the ends. It is filled with Red Bone Marrow.
Cartilage: A smooth, slippery tissue covering the ends. It acts as a shock absorber and reduces friction.

rows.valB: Can turn into Red marrow during blood loss

sections.title: Why do bones have nerves?
points: Nerves allow the bone to feel pain if it is injured or fractured.
This warns the body to stop moving and protect the injured area.

sections.text: Bones act as a Mineral Bank. If your blood levels of Calcium drop too low, the bones release calcium into the bloodstream to help other organs!

cards.fact: The factory for Red Blood Cells.
Stores fat and makes White Blood Cells.
cards.mnemonic: Fat is Yellow. Yellow marrow handles the fat!

cards.fact: The slippery 'cap' on the ends of bones.
cards.mnemonic: Cartilage is a Cushion for your bones!
